title: What each language's JSON parser can tell apart
pins: The distinctions an implementation's own JSON parser preserves. Every other suite here is generated by executing PHP, which means every other golden inherits PHP's expressiveness — and a golden cannot encode a distinction the language that produced it could not hold. This suite is the exception: its rows are RAW JSON TEXT, so the corpus can state a distinction the reference cannot compare, and each implementation answers for itself.

php.gap: jci-0001 is skipped: PHP decodes an empty JSON object and an empty JSON array to the identical value, so it cannot answer this row at all. That limit is not a defect, it is the reason this suite exists — and it is why no PHP-authored golden anywhere in this corpus is authoritative about container type. Finding F-3.

ts.gap: jci-0002 is skipped: JavaScript cannot represent integers above 2^53 and cannot detect that it cannot — the two sides of that row parse to the same double, and comparing the parsed value against the original literal returns true, so the language cannot see its own error even when asked directly. Finding F-5.
